[[File:航空神社(新橋).jpg|thumb|[[Kōkū Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)|Aviation Shrine in Minato, Tokyo]]]]
'''Kōkūjinja''' (航空神社) is a [[Shinto shrine|Shrine]] that uses “Aviation” as its name. All are famous for [[Aviation safety|Aviation Safety]] and travel safety.
Since the invention of the [[Airplane]], the frequency of [[Aviation accident]] has increased. As a result, many—starting with military personnel—became war dead [[Line of duty death|War Dead]], yet their spirits were not enshrined at [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. Therefore, to console these souls and honor their meritorious deeds at various units and schools, Aviation Shrines were established throughout the country.
== Shrines Bearing the Name "Aviation Shrine" ==
* [[Kōkū Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)|Aviation Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)]] – Located in [[Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]] [[Minato, Tokyo|Minato Ward]] and [[Shinbashi]], it is situated on the rooftop of the [[Japan Aeronautic Association]]’s Aviation Hall.
* [[Haneda Aviation Shrine]] – Located within the 1st Passenger Terminal of [[Haneda Airport|Tokyo International Airport]] (Haneda Airport) in Tokyo’s [[Ōta, Tokyo|Ota Ward]], this shrine was founded on [[July 11]], [[1963]] (Showa 38) by enshrining a branch spirit [[Bunrei|Branch Spirit]] through [[Bunrei|Enshrinement]] from the above Aviation Shrine. Formerly, the airport branch of [[Anamori Inari Shrine]] was also relocated nearby; however, during the terminal relocation in [[1993]] ([[Heisei era|Heisei]]5), it was merged into the main shrine.
* Aviation Shrine – Located in Akebonochō, [[Tachikawa, Tokyo|Tachikawa City]], Tokyo. It is said to have originated when a local influential person enshrined [[Kitano Tenmangu]] as a ward against unlucky directions, and later, at the request of the Army Air Force’s 5th Squadron, consolidated the aviation war dead.
* Aviation Shrine – Situated in Kawajiri, Midori Ward ([[Sagamihara|Sagamihara City]], [[Kanagawa Prefecture]]), this shrine was established to console the souls of fallen crew: on March 23, [[1941]] ([[Shōwa era|Showa]]16) a twin-engine reconnaissance aircraft crashed and burst into flames killing two crew members, and on April 8, [[1944]] (Showa 19) a Japanese Army Hayabusa fighter crashed with its pilot perishing.
* [[Sanctuaire de l'aviation (Tokorozawa)]] – Located at the [[Kitano Tenjinsha]] in [[Saitama Prefecture]] [[Tokorozawa, Saitama|Tokorozawa]], in the area of [[Kotesashi Motomachi]]. It was founded on September 25, Showa 12 by fulfilling the wish of [[Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi]], who, having received sacred wood from the construction of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] and materials from [[Hikawa Shrine (Saitama)|Hikawa Shrine]], built a shrine at the southern end of the [[Tokorozawa Airfield]] to enshrine [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] and to conduct ceremonies for the aviation war dead. At that time, because aviation war dead were not enshrined at [[Yasukuni Shrine]], they were venerated as protective deities of the nation. In Showa 13, the shrine was transferred to the premises of the [[Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|Army Aviation Officer School]] established in Toyooka (now part of the Japan Air Self-Defense Force’s [[Iruma Air Base|Iruma Base]]), becoming the center of reverence for its students. When the school grounds were seized by the U.S. military at the end of the war in Showa 20, aviation officials led by the school’s head [[Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi]] petitioned to preserve the shrine permanently. With the cooperation of local volunteers and the chief priest, Ryōsuke Kurihara, of the long-serving [[Kitano Tenjinsha]], the enshrinement was transferred in its original form on September 3, Showa 20, to the current [[Kitano Tenjinsha]]. Ceremonies have continued unceasingly ever since, with visits from local citizens, Prince Higashikuni, the governor of Saitama Prefecture, the mayor of Tokorozawa, successive heads of the Army Aviation Officer School, and Japan’s first official domestic flight pioneer, Tokugawa Yoshitoshi. After the establishment of the Air Self-Defense Force in 1954 (Showa 29), war dead personnel were enshrined at this Aviation Shrine (with branch enshrinements following the construction of the Defense Agency Memorial Monument). On November 19, [[1965]] (Showa 40), the spirit tablet was transferred to the Air Self-Defense Force Candidate School, then on February 26, [[1988]] (Showa 63) to the Air Self-Defense Force Iruma Base Shūbudai Memorial Hall. On March 13, [[2024]] (Reiwa 6), the spirit tablet was again transferred and enshrined at Kitano Tenmangu, and from April 13, [[2024]] (Reiwa 6) onward, the issuance of goshuin and aviation safety charms began.
* [[Museum of Aeronautical Science|Aviation Science Museum]] – Located within the premises of the Aviation Science Museum in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Sanbu District]], [[Shibayama, Chiba|Shibayama Town]], and [[Iwayama]], this shrine was originally established in [[1937]] (Showa 12) by aviation pioneer [[Otojirô Itô|Itō Otojirō]] to enshrine the war dead of the early aviation era—including his eldest son Shintarō and the celebrated aviator [[Yamagata Toyotaro]]—at the factory premises ([[Factory]] and [[site]]) of [[Itō Aircraft Manufacturing]] in Tsudanuma, [[Chiba District, Chiba|Chiba District]]’s Tsudanuma Town (now part of [[Narashino]]) in Saginuma. Following Japan’s defeat ([[Surrender of Japan|Japan's War Defeat]]), Itō, forced out of the aviation industry, became a farmer in the eastern peak area of Toyama Village (now part of Narita City) in [[Tōyama]] through postwar development ([[Postwar Development]]). After some time, the local community decided to build a shrine, and on November 23, [[1953]] (Showa 28) the shrine was relocated. At that time, a new enshrinement of [[Ninomiya Sontoku]] was made from [[Hōtoku Ninomiya Shrine]] of [[Kanagawa Prefecture]]. Later, the shrine was renamed “Tōhō Shrine” and came to be revered by the local settlers as the guardian shrine ([[Ujigami]]) of their new community. However, with the construction of the new Tokyo International Airport (now [[Narita International Airport]]), in September 2001 (Heisei 13) at the request of Itō Otojirō’s family, the spirit of Ninomiya Sontoku was retained and transferred to the outdoor display area of the Aviation Science Museum in Shibayama Town, Sanbu District, Chiba Prefecture. The shrine’s [[Omamori|Amulet]] is available at the museum’s shop.
* [[Japan Aviation High School|Japan Air High School]] – Located in Utsutani, [[Kai, Yamanashi|Kai City]], [[Yamanashi Prefecture]], this shrine is enshrined within the campus of Japan Air High School.
* [[Japan Aviation High School Ishikawa]] – Located in Suuei, Mitsuimachi, [[Wajima, Ishikawa|Wajima City]], [[Ishikawa Prefecture]], this shrine is enshrined within the campus of Japan Air High School Ishikawa.
* [[Senshu Aviation Shrine]] – Located in Kamikawaya, [[Izumisano]], [[Osaka Prefecture]], this shrine was established by branching off from the [[Iwafune Shrine]] of the private municipality in [[Katano|Katano City]], on the occasion of constructing [[Kansai International Airport]]. It is dedicated to prayers for aviation safety and travel safety; its official name is “Senshu Iwafune Shrine.”
* [[Takayama Kouku Park]] – Located in Higashibun Otsu, [[Ayauta District, Kagawa|Ayauta District]], [[Ayagawa, Kagawa|Ayagawa Town]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]], this shrine was founded on December 16, [[1990]] (Heisei 2) in conjunction with the development of Takayama Aviation Park, prompted by airplanes flying over after the completion of [[Takamatsu Airport]], as a prayer for the safety of air transportation. Next to the shrine stand an Army Youth Aviator Memorial Monument, established by volunteers from Kagawa Prefecture, and an ancient local earth god’s shrine. Since its enshrinement, successive [[Minister of Transport of Japan]]s and [[Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism]] have visited, with commemorative tree plantings around it.
== Shrines Closely Associated with Aviation ==
* [[Konpira Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)]] – Located in [[Toranomon]], Minato Ward, Tokyo, it was established when [[Kyōgoku Takakazu]]—the feudal lord of [[Sanuki Province]] and the [[Marugame Domain]]—enshrined [[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Daigongen]] at his Edo residence.
* [[Anamori Inari Shrine]] – Located in [[Haneda, Ōta, Tokyo|Haneda]], Ota Ward, Tokyo. The area now occupied by [[Haneda Airport|Tokyo International Airport]] (specifically, [[Haneda Airport]]) was once part of the grounds and monzen town of this shrine until [[1945]] (Showa 20). Even before the opening of [[Tokyo Airfield]] in [[1931]] (Showa 6), during the [[Taishō era|Taisho Era]], there is an account of flight school trainees in the monzen praying for safety. It remains the shrine nearest to the airport and was originally founded to protect Haneda Airport ([[Suzuki Shinden]]) from disaster. As an airport-protecting shrine, it attracts prayers for safety from the aviation industry, related government agencies, and travelers. Additionally, on the roof of the old Haneda Airport Terminal Building (prior to offshore expansion), both Haneda Aviation Shrine and the Anamori Inari Shrine Airport Branch were enshrined; even now, branch spirits are maintained on the grounds of the [[Japan Airlines|Japan Air Lines]] Main Maintenance Center and the [[San-Ai Oil|Sanei Oburi]] Haneda branch. {{Main|穴守稲荷神社#羽田空港（航空業界）との関係|qq=}}
* [[Ikazuchi Shrine(Yokosuka)]] – Located in [[Yokosuka|Yokosuka City]]’s [[Oppama-honchō]], Kanagawa Prefecture. In [[1938]] (Showa 13), following the establishment of the [[Yokohama Air Group|Yokohama Navy Air Corps]] in Tomioka, Kanazawa Ward, Yokohama, the [[Iseyama Kōtai Jingū]] was enshrined to create Torifune Shrine. After being seized by the U.S. military post-war and released in [[1971]] (Showa 46), the comrades association “Hamakū-kai” restored the damaged Torifune Shrine and, as “Hamakū Shrine,” held memorial services for fallen members. Eventually, due to aging, the association relocated the shrine building to [[Yokosuka Raijin Shrine]] in [[2008]] (Heisei 20) and erected a memorial monument inscribed with “Rest in Peace, Navy Seaplane Corps” on the former site.
* [[Fukami Shrine]] – Located in Fukami, [[Yamato, Kanagawa|Yamato City]], Kanagawa Prefecture, this shrine is the subsidiary of [[Fukami Shrine]]. It was once enshrined within the [[Atsugi Navy Air Corps Base]] (currently [[Naval Air Facility Atsugi]]) and was known as Atsugi Air Shrine, enshrining the war dead register of the Atsugi Navy Air Corps along with a treasured sword bestowed by Yasukuni Shrine.
* [[Tōhō Shrine]] – Located in [[Narita, Chiba|Narita City]]’s [[Tōhō]], Chiba Prefecture, it is set within the grounds of the Aviation Science Museum, where Ninomiya Sontoku was enshrined alongside the spirit of the Aviation Shrine. In [[2001]] (Heisei 13), the spirit of the Aviation Shrine was transferred to the museum’s outdoor display area in [[Iwayama]], Shibayama Town, Sanbu District, Chiba Prefecture.
* Hyakuri Shrine – Located in Yamano, [[Omitama|Komidama City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], it originally served as the guardian deity shrine for the Imperial Navy’s [[Hyakuri Naval Air Corps]] (linked with [[Imperial Japanese Navy|Imperial Navy]]).
* [[Yasuzumi Shrine]] – Situated in Kamitakanezawa, [[Takanezawa, Tochigi|Takanezawa Town]], [[Shioya District, Tochigi|Shioya District]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]], its grounds feature a [[Heliport|Helipad]] ([[off-site landing site]]).
* [[Isesaki Shrine]] – Located in [[Honmachi]], [[Isesaki|Isesaki City]], [[Gunma Prefecture]], this shrine houses a propeller that was dedicated by employees of [[Nakajima Aircraft Company|Nakashima Aircraft]] (later Fuji Heavy Industries, now [[Subaru Corporation|SUBARU]]) in prayer for safe returns from the battlefield. This propeller has influenced the design of goshuin and amulets for travel and aviation safety.
* Toriya Shrine – Located in Hagurochō, [[Ishinomaki|Ishinomaki City]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]], it is famous for its goshuin book associated with the [[Blue Impulse]].
* [[Shimomasuda Shrine]] – Situated at the Shimomasuda Mansion in [[Natori, Miyagi|Natori City]], Miyagi Prefecture, it enshrines an aviation shrine originally established in [[1939]] (Showa 14) at the former [[Sendai Army Flying School]].
* [[Mizobata Shrine]] – Located in Mizonokibacho, [[Gifu|Gifu City]], [[Gifu Prefecture]], this shrine is a subsidiary of [[Mizobata Shrine]]. It was founded on November 13, [[1944]] (Showa 19) within the Second Education Unit of the [[Gifu Army Aviation Maintenance School]], enshrined as the guardian for students of aviation technology, later transferred to the grounds of Mizonokiba Shrine, and eventually merged with the spirits of the school’s graduates (boy pilots).
* [[Asahi Inari Shrine]] – Located in [[Kakamigahara|Kakamigahara City]]’s [[Unuma Asahimachi]], Gifu Prefecture, this shrine was established as an aviation shrine at the Imperial Japanese Army’s base (displayed as [[Gifu Air Field|Gifu Base]]) and was later renamed when relocated after the war.
* [[Kuga Shrine]] – Located in Shichikitanakedera-chō, [[Kita-ku, Kyoto|Kita Ward]], Kyoto City, [[Kyoto Prefecture]], this shrine is an affiliate of [[Kamigamo Shrine|Kamobetsu Raijin Shrine]] and enshrines Kamo Tatemune of the [[Kamo clan|Kamo Clan]] (associated with [[Yatagarasu]]). It is especially venerated for conferring benefits in “traffic safety” and “aviation safety.”
* [[Hikō Shrine]] – Located in Hachiman Doi, [[Yawata|Yawata City]], Kyoto Prefecture, it was founded in [[1915]] (Taisho 4) by [[Chūhachi Ninomiya|Ninomiya Tada-hachi]], the first in Japan to study the principles of flight. Pained by the frequent aviation accidents since the invention of the airplane, he felt responsible for memorializing the victims of such tragedies and invested his personal funds to enshrine their spirits. It now attracts many visitors from the aviation and aerospace sectors seeking safety prayers.
* [[Iwafune Shrine]] – Located in the private municipality of [[Katano|Katano City]], Osaka Prefecture, this shrine enshrines the god of airplanes, [[Nigihayahi]], and also houses the enshrined spirits of aviation disaster victims ([[Enshrinement Together]]).
* [[Yata ni Imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine]] – Situated in Yata Town, [[Yamatokōriyama|Yamato-Koriyama]], [[Nara Prefecture]], the deity enshrined here, Kushidama Nigihayahi, is revered as the progenitor of aviation based on the legend recorded in the [[Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi]], which tells of him riding on a heavenly Iwafune and flying through the sky. An aviation festival is held every September 20, and a dedicated propeller hangs from the loft of the gatehouse.
* Kamikaze Shrine – Located in [[Nishinomiya|Nishinomiya City]]’s [[Uegahara]], Hyōgo Prefecture, it once served as the in-house shrine of the [[Nishinomiya Navy Air Corps]]. Before the post-war incineration, local residents risked their lives to relocate it into [[Kamigahara Hachiman Shrine]].
* [[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] – Located in Kawanishi, Kotohira Town, [[Nakatado District, Kagawa|Nakatado District]], Kagawa Prefecture, it is revered as the god of safe navigation and maritime protection, with its veneration later extending to land, sea, and aviation traffic safety.
* Ninomiya Flying Shrine – Situated in [[Mannō, Kagawa|Mannou Town]], Nakatado District, Kagawa Prefecture, at Oitsugi near [[Mominoki Pass]], it was founded in [[1991]] (Heisei 3) at the site where Tada-hachi is said to have first conceived the principles of flight.
